subtitle: Climb Mount Niitaka
photoCredit: Crew on the flight deck of the carrier Akagi, Hitokappu Bay, November 1941. Japanese photo, public domain (Wikimedia Commons).
body:
Three words go out by radio this evening, and the carriers steaming east know exactly what they mean.

"Niitakayama nobore 1208." Climb Mount Niitaka, the highest peak in the Empire. The number is the date: hostilities begin on 8 December, Tokyo time. In Hawaii that is Sunday, 7 December.

The signal reaches every unit of the Imperial Japanese Navy. Aboard the warships, sealed orders are opened. Only a recall can stop them now.
